I am Old Wang, 45 years old, farming these 6 mu in Quzhou for 15 years now. Let me think about this year.

My land is split between winter wheat and summer maize — that is what everyone does here, two crops one year on the same ground. 6 mu is not big, not small. With 7 people in the house, the grain mostly feeds us and the pigs; only a little gets sold. Every bag of fertilizer costs real money, so I cannot be careless, but I also cannot afford a bad harvest.

For wheat, I planted Jimai 22 last year — neighbor Old Liu got good yield from it, around 450 kg/mu, so I stick with it. I use the compound fertilizer 15-15-15, two bags (100 kg) per mu as base before planting, then top-dress with urea about 15 kg/mu at jointing stage. That gives me roughly 22 kg N, 15 kg P, 15 kg K per mu. I irrigate 3 times — before winter, jointing, and grain-filling. The well water is reliable. I spray pesticide twice, once for aphids and once for rust if I see it. I plough before wheat, deep plough every 2-3 years, rotary in between. This year I'll rotary since I ploughed last autumn.

For maize, I go with Zhengdan 958, a hybrid everyone trusts. I direct-seed no-till into the wheat stubble right after harvest — saves time, saves money on tillage. Base fertilizer one bag of compound (50 kg/mu) at sowing, then urea 20 kg/mu at big flare stage. That's about 18 kg N, 7.5 kg P, 7.5 kg K. Maize eats nitrogen heavily so I put more urea on top. Irrigate twice — after sowing if no rain, and at tasseling. One pesticide spray for corn borer. Expect around 550 kg/mu, neighbors get similar.
